skill.name: managing-projects
skill.description: Manage GitHub Projects v2 boards with GitHub CLI and GraphQL guidance for fields, views, items, templates, validation, and reports.
skill.summary: Plan, build, and maintain GitHub Projects v2 boards with CLI and GraphQL workflows.
skill.author: C0ntr0lledCha0s

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown examples, GraphQL identifiers, /dev/null redirects, and quoted GitHub CLI helper calls. Confirmed risks remain in privileged GitHub CLI installation guidance and an eval-based retry wrapper in scripts/project-helpers.sh. No prompt injection text or credential exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.suggestion: Remove auto-install language and require explicit user approval before any sudo, package manager, or curl-based installation step.
Replace eval in execute_with_retry with array-based command execution, or remove the unused wrapper entirely.
Add confirmation and dry-run review steps before creating projects, updating fields, archiving items, or bulk adding issues.

content.value_statement: GitHub Projects v2 requires GraphQL, CLI commands, and many IDs that are hard to manage by hand. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through project setup, field updates, validation, and reporting.
actual_capabilities: Creates GitHub Projects v2 boards and applies sprint, Kanban, roadmap, or bug triage templates.
Adds issues and pull requests to project boards with GitHub CLI workflows.
Builds and updates custom fields such as Status, Priority, Size, Sprint, and Due Date.
Queries project IDs, item IDs, field IDs, and option IDs through GraphQL examples.
Validates board configuration and reports missing fields, views, and orphaned items.
Generates project progress summaries from project item and field data.
limitations: Requires an authenticated GitHub CLI session and permissions for the target user or organization.
Uses GitHub network APIs and can change real project board data.
Advanced automation and view configuration may require manual GitHub settings.
Several helper workflows assume Unix shell tools such as jq, bash, grep, and awk.

use_cases.title: Create Team Delivery Boards
use_cases.description: Set up sprint or Kanban boards with consistent fields, statuses, and item workflows.

use_cases.title: Organize Repository Work
use_cases.description: Bulk add issues and pull requests to a project, then assign status and priority fields.

use_cases.title: Audit Project Hygiene
use_cases.description: Check whether boards have required fields, useful views, and linked project items.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Board
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a GitHub Projects v2 Kanban board for OWNER. Include Status and Priority fields and explain each step before making changes.

prompt_templates.title: Add Work Items
prompt_templates.prompt: Add open issues with LABEL from OWNER/REPO to project NUMBER. Confirm the search filter and owner before running commands.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a Project
prompt_templates.prompt: Review project NUMBER for OWNER. Report missing fields, weak views, orphaned items, and recommended fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Automate Sprint Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a sprint workflow for OWNER using GitHub Projects v2. Include field IDs, status transitions, bulk updates, and rollback guidance.

output_examples.input: Create a sprint planning board for my organization.
output: The skill proposes a sprint board with Status, Priority, Story Points, and Sprint fields.
It asks for owner confirmation before creating the project or changing GitHub data.
It returns the project ID and next steps for adding issues.

output_examples.output: The skill summarizes missing fields, empty views, orphaned items, and practical fixes in a concise audit report.

output_examples.input: Move high priority issues into the active board.
output_examples.output: The skill confirms the label filter, lists the target project, adds matching issues, and reports how many items changed.

best_practices: Confirm the GitHub owner, repository, and project number before running mutating commands.
Use dry-run style review steps before bulk adding, archiving, or updating project items.
Store important project IDs and field IDs so later GraphQL updates are repeatable.
anti_patterns: Running privileged installation commands from the skill without explicit user approval.
Bulk changing project items before verifying the issue search filter.
Using copied field IDs across projects without rechecking that they belong to the target board.

faq.question: Does this skill require GitHub CLI?
faq.answer: Yes. Most workflows require gh to be installed, authenticated, and authorized for project access.

faq.question: Can it manage organization projects?
faq.answer: Yes. It can work with user or organization projects when the authenticated account has permission.

faq.question: Does it use GraphQL?
faq.answer: Yes. GitHub Projects v2 uses GraphQL for many field, item, and project operations.

faq.question: Can it change real project data?
faq.answer: Yes. Creation, update, archive, and bulk add workflows can modify GitHub Projects data.

faq.question: Can it create custom fields?
faq.answer: Yes. The helper guidance covers single select, text, number, date, and iteration style project fields.

faq.question: Is it safe to use without review?
faq.answer: No. Review commands first because the skill can run GitHub CLI operations and includes privileged setup guidance.
